pr_title: ACMEAccount.get_request check status code value lower boundary
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
Any HTTP code below 200 cannot be considered a success, should be
handled like a failure instead.

This is particularly true for below zero status codes.

This change is required to avoid `ACMEAccount.get_request` to consider any HTTP status code below `400` to be a success. In #63139 status `-1` is returned due to a `.netrc` file permission error, but the function does not report it as an error.

Fixes #63139
<!--- HINT: Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue -->

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->
- module_utils/acme

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
<!--- Include additional information to help people understand the change here -->
<!--- A step-by-step reproduction of the problem is helpful if there is no related issue -->

Thanks for spotting this!

Hmm, I didn't expect that `fetch_url` would actually return -1 instead of raising an error (either exception or `module.fail_json()`). (Looking at its code, it's not surprising that it does... The example in its docs is somewhat misleading in that regard.)

Anyway, I would fix it differently. `fail_on_error` is only intended to catch ACME errors (or server errors). I would catch codes `< 200` (and also codes between `300` and `399`) and handle them by raising `ModuleFailException("ACME request failed with unexpected result: {0}".format(info['status']))` (or something like that).

Even better would be distinguishing between `< 0` (also print `info['msg']`) and the other unexpected codes (0..100, 300..399, just mention that these are unexpected). Also, this should also be done in the other places `fetch_url` is used. It's probably best to write a function which processes `fetch_url`'s result and haves like this, and returns only when the status code is in `200..299` or `>= 400`.

(Also, a [changelog fragment](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/development_process.html#changelogs-how-to) is missing.)

Thank you for the quick review and the suggestions! I'm going to rework it following your considerations.  
(I surely missed the changelog fragment mention somewhere, where I could find it?)

@endorama thanks! You can find infos on how changelog fragments look like here: https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/development_process.html#changelogs-how-to Also, you can find plenty of examples here: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/tree/devel/changelogs/fragments Here is one example of a bugfix changelog for the ACME modules: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/changelogs/fragments/61693-acme-buypass-acme-v1.yml

I was wondering how to implement the function processing `fetch_url` results:
- should be added to `module_utils.urls`?
- I was thinking naming it `assert_fetch_url_success()`, would that make sense? The rationale is having a processing function its only purpose is to ensure `fetch_url` results are actual success.
- I would raise inside this function on any non-successful behaviour. Which exceptions should I use? Should I just raise `Exception`? I would expect raising `ModuleFailException` from within `module_utils` should be avoided

I was thinking of adding it directly after `fetch_url` call:
```python
        if get_only:
            # Perform unauthenticated GET
            resp, info = fetch_url(self.module, uri, method='GET', headers=headers)

			# better to use a try/catch and raise ModuleFailException?
			assert_fetch_url_success(resp, info)

            try:
                content = resp.read()
            except AttributeError:
                content = info.pop('body', None)
```

Meanwhile I added the changelog fragment, let me know if it's correct!

> I was wondering how to implement the function processing `fetch_url` results:
> 
>     * should be added to `module_utils.urls`?

I wouldn't, at least not for now. If it turns out that this is a common problem for `fetch_url` users, it would make sense. (Also, the `ModuleFailException` exception is only defined in module_utils/acme.py. Generic code would have to use `module.fail_json()`.)

>     * I was thinking naming it `assert_fetch_url_success()`, would that make sense? The rationale is having a processing function its only purpose is to ensure `fetch_url` results are actual success.

Fine for me.

>     * I would raise inside this function on any non-successful behaviour.

I would restrict it to non-HTTP failures. Callers of `fetch_url` are supposed to handle HTTP failures, but not necessarily other types of errors (like connection errors).

> Which exceptions should I use? Should I just raise `Exception`? I would expect raising `ModuleFailException` from within `module_utils` should be avoided

Please use `ModuleFailException` from module_utils/acme.py. That's what the ACME modules use internally to handle failures.

> I was thinking of adding it directly after `fetch_url` call:
> 
> ```python
>         if get_only:
>             # Perform unauthenticated GET
>             resp, info = fetch_url(self.module, uri, method='GET', headers=headers)
> 
> 			# better to use a try/catch and raise ModuleFailException?
> 			assert_fetch_url_success(resp, info)
> 
>             try:
>                 content = resp.read()
>             except AttributeError:
>                 content = info.pop('body', None)
> ```

Looks good to me.

> > * I would raise inside this function on any non-successful behaviour.
> 
> I would restrict it to non-HTTP failures. Callers of `fetch_url` are supposed to handle HTTP failures, but not necessarily other types of errors (like connection errors).

Ok, I forgot about the 3xx handling. How about having an optional `allow_redirect=False` and `allow_client_error=True` and `allow_server_error=True` options, which (if set to `False`) raise exceptions for 3xx, 4xx resp. 5xx statuses?
@endorama are you still working on this?

@felixfontein sorry for the delay! I added a commit with the relevant code. I'm having some trouble testing it locally, any suggestion or resource would be appreciated!   
Thanks

issue_context.title: ACMEAccount.get_request does not fails and returns status -1 due to wrong .netrc permissions
issue_context.body:
<!--- Verify first that your issue is not already reported on GitHub -->
<!--- Also test if the latest release and devel branch are affected too -->
<!--- Complete *all* sections as described, this form is processed automatically -->

##### SUMMARY
<!--- Explain the problem briefly below -->
I discovered an issue in the `ACMEAccount` `module_utils`. Due to wrong permissions on `.netrc` file, the `fetch_url` method returns status `-1`, which skip the error check and make function return as the call was successful.

This breaks `ACMEDirectory.__init__`, that reports an error in the ACME directory: `ACME directory does not seem to follow protocol ACME v2` (the same would happen with ACME v1 directory).

I was able to discover the issue by exploding the AnsiballZ, debugging [`ACMEAccount.get_request` method](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/66de3d429f2454f8491f0633bf4298f3703c5db3/lib/ansible/module_utils/acme.py#L619) and discovering on line 657 the failing check:
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/66de3d429f2454f8491f0633bf4298f3703c5db3/lib/ansible/module_utils/acme.py#L657

In this error case, the `info` dictionary had `status` value of `-1`:

```
{
    "url": "https: //acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory",
    "status": -1,
    "msg": "An unknown error occurred: ~/.netrc access too permissive: access permissions must restrict access to only the owner (/home/.../.netrc, line 3)",
    "exception": "Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/home/.../.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-1570199461.7-3341753761542/debug_dir/ansible/module_utils/urls.py", line 1359, in fetch_url
        unix_socket=unix_socket)
      File "/home/.../.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-1570199461.7-3341753761542/debug_dir/ansible/module_utils/urls.py", line 1257, in open_url
        use_gssapi=use_gssapi, unix_socket=unix_socket)
      File "/home/.../.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-1570199461.7-3341753761542/debug_dir/ansible/module_utils/urls.py", line 1090, in open
        rc = netrc.netrc(os.environ.get(\"NETRC\"))
      File "/home/.../.asdf/installs/python/3.7.2/lib/python3.7/netrc.py", line 30, in __init__
        self._parse(file, fp, default_netrc)
      File "/home/.../.asdf/installs/python/3.7.2/lib/python3.7/netrc.py", line 107, in _parse
        " the owner", file, lexer.lineno)
    netrc.NetrcParseError: ~/.netrc access too permissive: access permissions must restrict access to only the owner (/home/.../.netrc, line 3)
    "
}
```

This value is not intercepted by the error check, which expect failures to have status greater than 400.
